correctness.rationale: The cofactor affine-covariance identity makes the planar area ratio affine-invariant; every interior-centered triangle has a canonical (1,0),(0,1),(-p,-q) form. Three exact line-chord rational expressions integrate by explicit rational substitutions to a logarithmic identity, rewritten in barycentric coordinates. The derivative identities g'(1-t)=g'(t) and g' strictly decreasing on (0,1/2) imply strict majorization monotonicity for triples, including cases with one coordinate above 1/2. The area is strictly between 2 and 2+(8/3)ln2, uniquely maximized at the centroid, and approaches 2 along any boundary. Exact rational line intersections and numerical integrals independently corroborate, not replace, the proof.

value.rationale: The area of a planar intersection body changes under translation, with no automatic affine-center equality. This result exactly resolves the natural triangle family, converting all translation choices to a transparent barycentric scalar, proving strict majorization monotonicity, the unique centroid maximizer, and a sharp boundary limit. Its area profile and universal constant provide usable benchmarks for noncentrally symmetric intersection-body calculations and motivate higher-polytope analogues.
